prompt: The Liskov Substitution Principle (LSP) states that…
choices: Every subclass must override all parent methods
Subtypes must be substitutable for their base types without breaking program correctness
A class should have only one reason to change
Interfaces should be small and focused
explanation: LSP: wherever you use a base type, a subtype should work correctly in its place. A Square that extends Rectangle violates LSP if setting width independently breaks the area contract. LSP violations cause surprising bugs when polymorphism is used.
